1.word_for_word: triṃśe — in the thirtieth chapter; viraha-santapta-gopībhiḥ — by the gopīs scorched by separation; kṛṣṇa-mārgaṇam — the search for Kṛṣṇa; unmatta-vat — like madwomen; na niyatam — without fixed direction; bhramantībhiḥ vane vane — wandering from forest to forest; acakṣāṇāḥ — not seeing; apaśyantyaḥ — unable to behold him
1.translation: In the thirtieth chapter the gopīs, scorched by separation from Kṛṣṇa, search for him, wandering without fixed direction from forest to forest like women driven mad. ‘Acakṣāṇāḥ’ means that they could not see him.

2.word_for_word: gatyā — by his gait; anurāga-smitābhyām — by his affectionate smiles; vibhrama-īkṣitāni — sportive glances; sa-vilāsa-nirīkṣaṇāni — playful looks; manoramā ālāpāḥ — charming speech; vihārāḥ krīḍāḥ — pastimes and play; vibhramāḥ anye ca vilāsāḥ — his other graceful gestures; ramā-pateḥ gati-ādibhiḥ — by these qualities of the Lord of Ramā; ākṣiptāni ākṛṣṭāni cittāni yāsām — whose minds were seized and drawn away; tasmin eva ātmā yāsām — whose very selves were fixed in him; tasya vividhāḥ ceṣṭāḥ jagṛhuḥ — they adopted his various actions; tad-anukaraṇena akrīḍan — they played by imitating him
2.translation: Kṛṣṇa's gait, affectionate smiles, playful glances, charming speech, games and countless graceful gestures had completely drawn away their minds. Because their very selves were now fixed in him, they took on his different movements and pastimes and began to play by imitating him.

3.word_for_word: priyasya gati-ādiṣu pratirūḍhā āviṣṭā mūrtayaḥ yāsām — whose bodies were completely absorbed in the beloved's gait and other manners; kṛṣṇa-vihāra-vibhramāḥ — whose sports and gestures had become Kṛṣṇa's own; aham eva kṛṣṇaḥ iti — ‘I myself am Kṛṣṇa’; parasparam niveditavatyaḥ — they declared this to one another
3.translation: Their whole bodily bearing became absorbed in the gait and gestures of their beloved, so that their own play resembled Kṛṣṇa's play. In that absorption they even said to one another, ‘I am Kṛṣṇa himself.’

4.word_for_word: gāyantyaḥ — singing; vanāt vanāntaram gacchantyaḥ — going from one forest section to another; vicikyuḥ amṛgayan — they searched; unmatta-tulyatvam āha — their resemblance to madwomen is shown; vanaspatīn papracchuḥ — they questioned the trees; bhūteṣu antaram madhye santam puruṣam — the Puruṣa present within beings; bahiḥ ca santam — and present without
4.translation: Still singing of him, they moved from one part of the forest to another and searched. Their madness is shown by the fact that they began questioning the trees. The verse also alludes to the Puruṣa who is present both within all beings and outside them.

5.word_for_word: tat prapañcayati navabhiḥ — this questioning is elaborated in nine verses; mahattvāt ete paśyeyuḥ — thinking these great trees might have seen him; aśvattha-ādīn pṛcchanti — they ask the aśvattha and others; prema-hāsa-vilasitaiḥ avalokanaiḥ — with glances full of loving smiling play; asmākam manaḥ hṛtvā — having stolen our minds; cora iva gataḥ — he went away like a thief; vaḥ yuṣmābhiḥ kim dṛṣṭaḥ — did you see him
5.translation: Their questioning is expanded over the next verses. Thinking that the great aśvattha and other trees might have seen him, they ask: ‘He stole our minds with smiling, love-filled glances and slipped away like a thief. Did you see where he went?’

6.word_for_word: mahāntaḥ sva-puṣpaiḥ bahu-upakāriṇaḥ ca — these plants are noble and greatly beneficent through their flowers; kuravaka-ādīn pṛcchanti — they ask the kuravaka and others; darpa-haram smitam yasya — he whose smile destroys pride; itaḥ gataḥ — who passed this way; kaccit dṛṣṭaḥ — did you happen to see him
6.translation: Because the flowering shrubs such as kuravaka are generous benefactors through their blossoms, the gopīs ask them too: ‘Did you see him pass this way—him whose smile destroys all pride?’

7.word_for_word: ali-kulaiḥ saha — together with swarms of bees; tvām bibhrat — wearing/carrying you; tava ati-priyaḥ — he who is especially dear to you; tvayā kim dṛṣṭaḥ — have you seen him
7.translation: They ask Tulasī: ‘He carries you with him, surrounded by swarms of bees, and he is especially dear to you. Have you seen him?’

8.word_for_word: guṇa-atireke api namratvāt — because, despite their great qualities, these creepers are humble; imāḥ paśyeyuḥ iti — thinking they might have seen him; mālati mallike jāti yūthike — O mālatī, mallikā, jāti and yūthikā; vaḥ yuṣmābhiḥ kim adarśi — was he seen by you; kara-sparśena vaḥ prītim janayan — giving you joy by the touch of his hand; kim yātaḥ — did he pass this way; mālatī-jātyoḥ avāntara-viśeṣaḥ — mālatī and jāti are distinct subvarieties
8.translation: Thinking that these flowering creepers, humble despite their excellence, might have seen him, the gopīs ask: ‘O mālatī, mallikā, jāti and yūthikā, did you see him pass this way, delighting you with the touch of his hand?’ Śrīdhara notes that mālatī and jāti are distinct varieties.

9.word_for_word: phalādibhiḥ sarva-prāṇinām santarpakāḥ — satisfying all creatures with fruits and other gifts; cūta-ādayaḥ — mango and the other trees; cūta-āmrayoḥ avāntara-jāti-bhedaḥ — cūta and āmra are different mango varieties; kadamba-nīpayoḥ ca — likewise kadamba and nīpa; parārtha-bhavakāḥ — whose existence is solely for others; parārtham eva bhavaḥ janma yeṣām — whose birth serves others; yamunā-upakūlāḥ — standing near the bank of the Yamunā; tīrtha-vāsinaḥ — residents of a sacred place; rahita-ātmanām — of us whose minds/selves are lost; śūnya-cetasām — empty-hearted; kṛṣṇa-padavīm — Kṛṣṇa's path; śaṃsantu kathayantu — please tell us
9.translation: The gopīs next appeal to the fruit-bearing trees that nourish all creatures. Cūta and āmra are different mango varieties, and kadamba and nīpa likewise distinct. ‘O trees whose very birth exists for the sake of others, dwelling beside the sacred Yamunā, please tell us Kṛṣṇa's path, for our minds are gone and our hearts are empty without him.’

10.word_for_word: he kṣiti — O earth; tvayā kim tapaḥ kṛtam — what austerity have you performed; keśava-aṅghri-sparśa-utsavā — you whose festival is the touch of Keśava's feet; aṅga-ruhaiḥ utpulakitā — thrilled with hairs standing erect, manifested as grasses; vibhāsi — you shine; api kim ayam utsavaḥ aṅghri-sambhavaḥ adhunā — is this joy caused by his foot-touch just now; tava eka-deśa-aṅghri-sparśa-sambhūtaḥ — produced by his touching one portion of you; yad vā urukrama-vikramāt — or from the ancient stride of Trivikrama; pūrvam eva trivikramasya padā sarva-ākramaṇāt — when his foot covered you entirely; āho varāhasya vapuṣaḥ parirambhaṇena — or earlier still, from the embrace of Varāha's body; tvayā nūnam dṛṣṭaḥ — surely you have seen him; tam darśaya — show him to us
10.translation: They address the earth: ‘O Earth, what austerity did you perform to obtain the festival of Keśava's foot-touch? You shine covered with grasses like hairs standing on end. Is this ecstasy from his touching you here just now? Or has it remained since Trivikrama strode over your whole body? Or perhaps from still earlier, when Varāha embraced you? Surely you have seen our Kṛṣṇa—show us where he went.’

11.word_for_word: hariṇyā dṛṣṭi-pratyāsattyā — because the doe's sight reaches nearby; kṛṣṇa-darśanam sambhāvya — supposing she may have seen Kṛṣṇa; he sakhi eṇa-patni — O friend, wife of the deer; api kim upagataḥ — did he come nearby; gātraiḥ sundaraiḥ mukha-bāhu-ādibhiḥ — with his beautiful face, arms and limbs; priyayā saha — together with his beloved; tatra dyotakam — the sign of this is; kāntāyā aṅga-saṅgaḥ — contact with the beloved's body; tat-kuca-kuṅkumena rañjitāyāḥ kunda-kusuma-srajaḥ gandhaḥ — the fragrance of his jasmine garland colored by kuṅkuma from her breasts; kulapateḥ śrī-kṛṣṇasya — of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, chief of the clan; vāti āgacchati — the scent is carried here by the wind
11.translation: Thinking a nearby doe may have seen him, they say, ‘O friend, wife of the deer, did Kṛṣṇa come near here with his beautiful face and limbs, together with his beloved?’ They imagine a sign: the breeze carries the fragrance of Kṛṣṇa's jasmine garland, now colored by the kuṅkuma from the breasts of the beloved who embraced him.

12.word_for_word: phala-bhāreṇa natān tarūn — trees bent beneath fruit; kṛṣṇam dṛṣṭvā praṇatā iti matvā — imagining they bow because they saw Kṛṣṇa; priyayā saha tasya gati-vilāsam sambhāvayantyaḥ — supposing he passed playfully with his beloved; tulasikāyā ali-kulaiḥ — with swarms of bees around Tulasī; tat-āmoda-mada-andhaiḥ — intoxicated and blinded by her fragrance; anvīyamānaḥ anugamyamānaḥ — followed by them; iha caran — wandering here
12.translation: Seeing trees bent low with the weight of their fruit, the gopīs imagine they are bowing because Kṛṣṇa passed by with his beloved. ‘Did he wander here,’ they ask, ‘followed by swarms of bees intoxicated by the fragrance of his Tulasī garland?’

13.word_for_word: imā latāḥ kṛṣṇena saṅgatā nūnam — these creepers surely met Kṛṣṇa; imāḥ pṛcchata — ask them; sva-pati-saṅgatau tat-saṅgatiḥ durghaṭā iti na — their being embraced by their own tree-husbands does not exclude contact with Kṛṣṇa; vanaspateḥ patyuḥ bāhunā āśliṣṭāḥ api — although clasped by the branches of their tree-husbands; aho bhāgyam nūnam tat-nakhaiḥ spṛṣṭāḥ — surely they were fortunate enough to be touched by his nails; yataḥ utpulakāni bibhrati — because they display such ecstatic sprouts/gooseflesh; na hi sva-pati-saṅgatau īdṛk-pulaka-sambhavaḥ — ordinary contact with their own husbands would not produce such ecstasy
13.translation: Some gopīs say, ‘Friends, these creepers have surely met Kṛṣṇa—ask them!’ Although the creepers are already embraced by the branch-arms of their tree-husbands, that does not explain their extraordinary ecstasy. ‘They must have been touched by Kṛṣṇa's nails, for mere contact with their own husbands could never produce sprouts like hairs standing on end in this way.’

14.word_for_word: unmattavat papracchuḥ iti etat prapañcitam — the account of their questioning like madwomen has been completed; ramā-pateḥ tās tā viceṣṭā jagṛhuḥ tad-ātmikāḥ iti yad uktam — now Śuka elaborates the earlier statement that, becoming absorbed in the Lord of Ramā, they adopted his various acts; unmatta-vacaḥ gopyaḥ — the gopīs spoke like madwomen; kṛṣṇasya anveṣaṇena kātarāḥ — distressed by searching for Kṛṣṇa; ati-vihvalāḥ — utterly overwhelmed; anucakruḥ — they imitated him
14.translation: The description of their mad questioning is now complete. Śuka next expands his earlier statement that, absorbed in the Lord of Ramā, they enacted his various deeds. Overwhelmed and distraught from searching for Kṛṣṇa, the gopīs spoke and acted like madwomen, imitating his pastimes.

15.word_for_word: caturbhiḥ anukaraṇam prapañcyate — four verses elaborate their imitation; pūtanāyantyāḥ — of one acting like Pūtanā; pūtanāvat ācarantyāḥ — behaving as Pūtanā did; kṛṣṇavat ācarantī — another acting as Kṛṣṇa; stanam apibat — sucked her breast; tokāyitvā — making herself into a baby; tokavat ātmānam kṛtvā — assuming the role of an infant
15.translation: The next four verses describe their imitation of Kṛṣṇa's earlier pastimes. One gopī acted like Pūtanā, while another became Kṛṣṇa and, making herself into an infant, imitated sucking Pūtanā's breast.

16-17.word_for_word: daityāyitvā — acting as a demon; daityavat tṛṇāvartavat ātmānam kṛtvā — taking the role of the demon Tṛṇāvarta; ekā — one gopī; kṛṣṇa-arbha-bhāvanām — another imagining herself to be Kṛṣṇa as a little child; tām anyām jahāra — carried that other one away
16-17.translation: One gopī took the role of the demon Tṛṇāvarta, while another imagined herself to be the infant Kṛṣṇa; the first then carried the second away in imitation of that pastime.

18.word_for_word: dūragāḥ — cows standing far away; yadvad yathā kṛṣṇaḥ — as Kṛṣṇa would do; āhūya — calling them; tam kṛṣṇam anuvartamānām — another gopī following/imitating Kṛṣṇa; anukurvatīm iti vā pāṭhaḥ — variant reading: ‘imitating him’
18.translation: ‘Dūragāḥ’ means cows standing at a distance. One gopī called them just as Kṛṣṇa would, while another followed Kṛṣṇa's manner; a variant reading explicitly says that she ‘imitated’ him.

20.word_for_word: yatantī — making an effort; prayatnam kurvatī — striving; ambaram — her upper garment; uttarīyam vastram — the cloth worn above; unnidadhe — she raised it; ūrdhvam dhṛtavatī — held it overhead
20.translation: One gopī, imitating Kṛṣṇa lifting Govardhana, made a show of effort and held her upper garment aloft.

22.word_for_word: apidadhvam — cover them; nimīlayata — close your eyes
22.translation: ‘Apidadhvam’ means ‘cover/close them,’ that is, ‘shut your eyes.’

23.word_for_word: sudṛk — beautiful-eyed; su-nayanam āsyam pidhāya — covering her beautiful-eyed face; sudṛk vara-akṣī iti vā — alternatively, ‘the beautiful-eyed woman’; bhīti-viḍambanam — imitation of fear; bhaya-anukaraṇam — acting out being frightened
23.translation: One beautiful-eyed gopī covered her face and imitated the fear of those protected by Kṛṣṇa. ‘Bhīti-viḍambanam’ means a dramatic imitation of fear.

24.word_for_word: punar api vṛndāvane — again in Vṛndāvana; latāḥ tarūn ca kṛṣṇam pṛcchantyaḥ — asking the creepers and trees about Kṛṣṇa; vana-uddeśe vana-pradeśe — in a particular part of the forest; vyacakṣata — they saw/discerned something
24.translation: Again they moved through Vṛndāvana asking the creepers and trees about Kṛṣṇa. In one particular forest tract they suddenly perceived signs of his passage.

26.translation: ‘Supṛktāni’ means that the two sets of footprints were closely joined and intermixed.

27.word_for_word: tena aṃse nyastaḥ prakoṣṭhaḥ yasyāḥ — she whose forearm was placed upon his shoulder; kareṇoḥ hastinyāḥ — like the trunk/forelimb of a she-elephant
27.translation: The marks suggest a woman whose forearm rested upon Kṛṣṇa's shoulder, like a she-elephant leaning upon her mate.

28.word_for_word: rahaḥ — private place; ekānta-sthānam — a secluded spot

29.word_for_word: he ālyaḥ sakhyaḥ — O friends; aho dhanyāḥ ati-puṇyāḥ — how blessed and supremely holy; govinda-aṅghri-abja-reṇavaḥ — the dust from Govinda's lotus feet; yān — which even the great ones worship; asmābhiḥ api etat-reṇu-abhiṣekeṇa — if we too bathe ourselves in that dust; tathaiva kṛṣṇaḥ prāptum śakyaḥ — perhaps Kṛṣṇa can be attained in the same way
29.translation: ‘O friends, how blessed—how supremely sacred—is the dust of Govinda's lotus feet!’ Their thought is that if they too anoint or bathe themselves in this dust, perhaps they can attain Kṛṣṇa just as the fortunate beloved walking with him has done.

30.word_for_word: gopīnām sarvāsām — of all the gopīs; bhavet evam yadi tasyāḥ padāni sampṛktāni na bhaveyuḥ — this hope would be possible if that woman's footprints were not mingled with his; tāni tu naḥ duḥkham kurvanti — but those mixed footprints cause us pain; tat-pada-rajaḥ-sevanam kṛṣṇa-prāpti-sādhanam bhavet — service to his foot-dust would be a means to attain Kṛṣṇa; tasyāḥ pāda-rajasā miśritatvāt — but his dust is mingled with the dust of her feet
30.translation: Another gopī replies: ‘That would be so if her footprints were not mingled with his. We could then worship Kṛṣṇa's foot-dust alone as the means of reaching him. But seeing his dust mixed everywhere with the dust of this one woman's feet only increases our pain.’

31.word_for_word: tad-asampṛktān kevalam kṛṣṇa-pāda-reṇūn eva vicinvantyaḥ — searching for places where only Kṛṣṇa's footprints appeared unmixed; tān dṛṣṭvā — seeing them; punar atyantam samatapan — they became even more distressed; na lakṣyante iti — beginning ‘they are no longer visible’; khidyatī sujāte sukumāre aṅghri-tale yasyāḥ — she whose delicately born feet were becoming sore; tām unninye — he lifted her; skandham āropitavān — placed her upon his shoulder
31.translation: The gopīs searched for places where Kṛṣṇa's footprints continued alone. When they found them, however, they became even more distressed. The marks indicated that the delicate feet of the woman accompanying him had grown sore, so Kṛṣṇa lifted her and carried her upon his shoulder.

33.word_for_word: prapadābhyām ākramaṇam — pressure from the foreparts of his feet; kṣauṇī-mardanam — pressing into the earth; yayoḥ — in these footprints; ata eva asakale pade paśyata — therefore notice that the footprints are incomplete
33.translation: The partial impressions show that Kṛṣṇa pressed mainly with the front portions of his feet, as one does while reaching upward. ‘Look,’ they say, ‘the footprints are therefore incomplete.’

34.word_for_word: tasyāḥ kṛṣṇa-jānu-antar-upaviṣṭāyāḥ cihnam — signs that she sat between Kṛṣṇa's knees; keśa-prasādhanam — he arranged her hair; kāntām adhikṛtya — attending to his beloved; tāni prasūnāni cūḍayatā — placing those flowers in her hair; cūḍā-anukāreṇa badhnatā — binding them as a coiffure; dhruvam upaviṣṭam — he must certainly have sat here
34.translation: From the marks they conclude that the woman sat between Kṛṣṇa's knees while he dressed her hair. He must have sat in that spot while arranging the gathered flowers into her coiffure.

35.word_for_word: reme iti-ādi śuka-uktiḥ — the statement beginning ‘he enjoyed’ is Śuka's narration; ātma-rataḥ — delighting in himself; svataḥ tuṣṭaḥ — satisfied in himself; ātmārāmaḥ — self-sporting; akhaṇḍitaḥ — unbroken, unaffected; strī-vibhramaiḥ anākṛṣṭaḥ api — although not attracted or conquered by feminine charms; kim iti reme — why then did he sport; kāminām iti — the next phrase explains it: for the sake of those overcome by desire
35.translation: The statement ‘he enjoyed with her’ is Śuka's own narration. Kṛṣṇa is ‘ātma-rata,’ satisfied in himself, and ‘ātmārāma,’ one whose play is within his own Self; he remains unconquered by feminine charms. Why then does he enact such enjoyment? The phrase concerning ‘those who are lustful’ explains that his līlā serves a teaching purpose concerning the nature and wretchedness of worldly desire.

37.word_for_word: strīṇām durātmatām āha — the text exposes the fault that arose in the chosen woman's mind; kāmaḥ yānam āgamana-sādhanam yāsām — the other gopīs had desire itself as the vehicle that brought them; tā gopīḥ hitvā — he abandoned all those gopīs; mām bhajate iti hetoḥ — because ‘he has chosen me’; ātmānam variṣṭham mene — she considered herself superior
37.translation: The chosen gopī's subtle fault is now described. All the women had been carried to Kṛṣṇa by the same intense love, yet because he left the others and remained with her, she began to think, ‘He has chosen me,’ and regarded herself as the best of them.

39.word_for_word: kāminām dainyam darśayati — he demonstrates the pitiable condition produced by proud desire; evam ukte — when she spoke thus; akhaṇḍitatvam āha — Kṛṣṇa's independence is shown; tasyām skandha-āroha-udyatāyām — just as she was preparing to mount his shoulder; antarhitaḥ — he disappeared
39.translation: The episode demonstrates how pitiable desire becomes when mixed with pride, while also showing Kṛṣṇa's complete independence. At the very moment she prepared to climb upon his shoulder, he disappeared.

40.word_for_word: anutāpam āha — her remorse is expressed; hā nātha iti — in the cry ‘Alas, my Lord!’
40.translation: Her remorse and despair are expressed in the cry, ‘Alas, my Lord!’

41.word_for_word: anvicchantyaḥ — searching; mṛgayamāṇāḥ — seeking him; avidūrataḥ — not far away; samīpe — nearby
41.translation: The other gopīs, still searching for Kṛṣṇa, found her nearby.

42.source_note: The electronic Śrīdhara source contains only ‘???’ for this entry, so no translation is supplied.
42.word_for_word: [source illegible] — the electronic source is missing here
42.translation: [Śrīdhara's text is illegible or absent in the electronic source for this verse.]

43.word_for_word: tataḥ tayā api sahitāḥ — then joined by that gopī as well; kṛṣṇa-anveṣaṇāya vanam aviśan — they entered the forest again to search for Kṛṣṇa; tataḥ asya eva hareḥ anveṣaṇāt nivṛttāḥ — eventually they ceased physically searching for this same Hari; gauḍīya-ṭīkākṛdbhiḥ atra asya eva iti paṭhyate — Gauḍīya commentators read ‘asyaiva’ here
43.translation: Joined now by that gopī as well, they re-entered the forest in search of Kṛṣṇa. Eventually they ceased the outward search for Hari. Śrīdhara's source notes that Gauḍīya commentators read ‘asyaiva’ at this point.

44.word_for_word: evam tam aprāptā api — although they still had not found him; sva-gṛhān na eva smṛtavatyaḥ — they never even remembered their homes; tad-ātmikāḥ — having him as their very self; saḥ eva ātmā yāsām — he alone was their self; tan-mayyaḥ — wholly filled with him
44.translation: Even after failing to find Kṛṣṇa, they did not once remember their homes. They had become ‘tad-ātmikāḥ’: Kṛṣṇa alone was their very self, and their consciousness was wholly filled with him.

45.word_for_word: pūrvam yatra śrī-kṛṣṇena saṅgatiḥ āsīt — the place where they had earlier been together with Śrī Kṛṣṇa; tad eva kālindyāḥ pulinam āgatya — returning to that same sandbank of the Yamunā; kṛṣṇam bhāvayanti dhyāyanti — they contemplated and meditated upon him; kṛṣṇasya āgamanam kāṅkṣitam yāsām — all longing for his return; militāḥ satyaḥ — gathered together; kṛṣṇam eva jaguḥ — they sang only of Kṛṣṇa
45.translation: Instead they returned to the very Yamunā sandbank where they had earlier enjoyed Kṛṣṇa's company. There they contemplated and meditated upon him. United in longing for his return, they gathered together and sang of Kṛṣṇa alone.
